name: Headlines Only
description: Write only the slide headlines as full claims and read them in order as the whole talk.
key_questions: Does the arc make sense from headlines alone?|Which headline is a label, not a claim?|Which slide is missing between two headlines?

name: One Picture Per Idea
description: For each slide, name the single picture that proves its headline.
key_questions: If this slide could show only one thing, what would it be?|Is that a number, a comparison, a sequence, or a scene?|What would you delete to make room for it?

name: The Hero Number
description: Find the one figure that makes the problem undeniable and give it a slide to itself.
key_questions: Which number would make the room go quiet?|Compared with what?|Is it real and sourced?

name: Before and After
description: Show the same thing in two states side by side.
key_questions: What does it look like today?|What does it look like after?|What single change explains the difference?

name: Build the Diagram
description: Reveal a process or model one step at a time instead of all at once.
key_questions: What is the first piece the audience needs?|What does each step add?|Where does the payoff appear?

name: The Visual Metaphor
description: Find an everyday image the audience already understands that carries the idea.
key_questions: What does this idea work like in ordinary life?|Would the audience get it in three seconds?|Where does the metaphor break, and does that matter?

name: The Three-Second Glance
description: Show each slide for three seconds and ask what someone took away.
key_questions: What would a glance take from this slide?|Is that the headline's point?|What is fighting for attention?

name: The Squint Test
description: Squint at the slide and check that the one important thing still stands out.
key_questions: What do you see first when you squint?|Is it the right thing?|What can fade back?
